units.leftText: God, having in the past spoken to the fathers through the prophets at many times and in various ways,
units.rightText: On many past occasions and in many different ways, God spoke to our fathers through the prophets.

units.leftText: has at the end of these days spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom also he made the worlds.
units.rightText: But in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, and through whom He made the universe.
rightNotes: 1:2 Or the world; literally the ages

units.leftText: His Son is the radiance of his glory, the very image of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power, who, when he had by himself purified us of our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high,
units.rightText: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word. After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

units.leftText: having become as much better than the angels as the more excellent name he has inherited is better than theirs.
units.rightText: So He became as far superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is excellent beyond theirs.

units.leftText: For to which of the angels did he say at any time, “You are my Son. Today I have become your father?” and again, “I will be to him a Father, and he will be to me a Son?”
units.rightText: For to which of the angels did God ever say: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father” ? Or again: “I will be His Father, and He will be My Son” ?
rightNotes: 1:5 Psalm 2:7|PSA 2:7*; literally today I have begotten You

units.leftText: When he again brings in the firstborn into the world he says, “Let all the angels of God worship him.”
units.rightText: And again, when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says: “Let all God’s angels worship Him.”

units.leftText: Of the angels he says, “He makes his angels winds, and his servants a flame of fire.”
units.rightText: Now about the angels He says: “He makes His angels winds, His servants flames of fire.”

units.leftText: But of the Son he says, “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever. The scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your Kingdom.
units.rightText: But about the Son He says: “Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.

units.leftText: You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows.”
units.rightText: You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, Your God, has anointed You above Your companions with the oil of joy.”

units.leftText: And, “You, Lord, in the beginning, laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the works of your hands.
units.rightText: And: “In the beginning, O Lord, You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.

units.leftText: They will perish, but you continue. They all will grow old like a garment does.
units.rightText: They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment.

units.leftText: You will roll them up like a mantle, and they will be changed; but you are the same. Your years won’t fail.”
units.rightText: You will roll them up like a robe; like a garment they will be changed; but You remain the same, and Your years will never end.”
rightNotes: 1:12 BYZ and TR do not include like a garment.

units.leftText: But which of the angels has he told at any time, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet?”
units.rightText: Yet to which of the angels did God ever say: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet” ?

units.leftText: Aren’t they all serving spirits, sent out to do service for the sake of those who will inherit salvation?
units.rightText: Are not the angels ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?

units.leftText: Therefore we ought to pay greater attention to the things that were heard, lest perhaps we drift away.
units.rightText: We must pay closer attention, therefore, to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.

units.leftText: For if the word spoken through angels proved steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just penalty,
units.rightText: For if the message spoken by angels was binding, and every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment,

units.leftText: how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation—which at the first having been spoken through the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard,
units.rightText: how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation?

units.leftText: God also testifying with them, both by signs and wonders, by various works of power, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit, according to his own will?
units.rightText: and was affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will. Jesus like His Brothers

units.leftText: For he didn’t subject the world to come, of which we speak, to angels.
units.rightText: For it is not to angels that He has subjected the world to come, about which we are speaking.

units.leftText: But one has somewhere testified, saying, “What is man, that you think of him? Or the son of man, that you care for him?
units.rightText: But somewhere it is testified in these words: “What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?

units.leftText: You made him a little lower than the angels. You crowned him with glory and honor.
units.rightText: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor
leftNotes: 2:7 TR adds “and set him over the works of your hands”
rightNotes: 2:7 Or a little while lower; also in verse 9
2:7 WH and TR include and set him over the works of Your hands.

units.leftText: You have put all things in subjection under his feet.” For in that he subjected all things to him, he left nothing that is not subject to him. But now we don’t yet see all things subjected to him.
units.rightText: and placed everything under his feet.”

units.leftText: But we see him who has been made a little lower than the angels, Jesus, because of the suffering of death crowned with glory and honor, that by the grace of God he should taste of death for everyone.
units.rightText: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death, so that by the grace of God He might taste death for everyone.

units.leftText: For it became him, for whom are all things and through whom are all things, in bringing many children to glory, to make the author of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
units.rightText: In bringing many sons to glory, it was fitting for God, for whom and through whom all things exist, to make the author of their salvation perfect through suffering.

units.leftText: For both he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one, for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brothers,
units.rightText: For both the One who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are of the same family. So Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers.
leftNotes: 2:11 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: saying, “I will declare your name to my brothers. Among the congregation I will sing your praise.”
units.rightText: He says: “I will proclaim Your name to My brothers; I will sing Your praises in the assembly.”

units.leftText: Again, “I will put my trust in him.” Again, “Behold, here I am with the children whom God has given me.”
units.rightText: And again: “I will put My trust in Him.” And once again: “Here am I, and the children God has given Me.”

units.leftText: Since then the children have shared in flesh and blood, he also himself in the same way partook of the same, that through death he might bring to nothing him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,
units.rightText: Now since the children have flesh and blood, He too shared in their humanity, so that by His death He might destroy him who holds the power of death, that is, the devil,

units.leftText: and might deliver all of them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.
units.rightText: and free those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death.

units.leftText: For most certainly, he doesn’t give help to angels, but he gives help to the offspring of Abraham.
units.rightText: For surely it is not the angels He helps, but the descendants of Abraham.

units.leftText: Therefore he was obligated in all things to be made like his brothers, that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.
units.rightText: For this reason He had to be made like His brothers in every way, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God, in order to make atonement for the sins of the people.

units.leftText: For in that he himself has suffered being tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted.
units.rightText: Because He Himself suffered when He was tempted, He is able to help those who are being tempted.

units.leftText: Therefore, holy brothers, partakers of a heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our confession: Jesus,
units.rightText: Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, set your focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.

units.leftText: who was faithful to him who appointed him, as also Moses was in all his house.
units.rightText: He was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as Moses was faithful in all God’s house.
rightNotes: 3:2 Literally just as Moses in all His house; SBL just as Moses in His house

units.leftText: For he has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, because he who built the house has more honor than the house.
units.rightText: For Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has greater honor than the house itself.

units.leftText: For every house is built by someone; but he who built all things is God.
units.rightText: And every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.

units.leftText: Moses indeed was faithful in all his house as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were afterward to be spoken,
units.rightText: Now Moses was faithful as a servant in all God’s house, testifying to what would be spoken later.

units.leftText: but Christ is faithful as a Son over his house. We are his house, if we hold fast our confidence and the glorying of our hope firm to the end.
units.rightText: But Christ is faithful as the Son over God’s house. And we are His house, if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope of which we boast. Do Not Harden Your Hearts (Psalm 95:1–11|PSA 95:1-11*)
rightNotes: 3:6 NE, WH, BYZ, and TR include to the end.

units.leftText: Therefore, even as the Holy Spirit says, “Today if you will hear his voice,
units.rightText: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: “Today, if you hear His voice,

units.leftText: don’t harden your hearts as in the rebellion, in the day of the trial in the wilderness,
units.rightText: do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion, in the day of testing in the wilderness,

units.leftText: where your fathers tested me and tried me, and saw my deeds for forty years.
units.rightText: where your fathers tested and tried Me, and for forty years saw My works.

units.leftText: Therefore I was displeased with that generation, and said, ‘They always err in their heart, but they didn’t know my ways.’
units.rightText: Therefore I was angry with that generation, and I said, ‘Their hearts are always going astray, and they have not known My ways.’

units.leftText: As I swore in my wrath, ‘They will not enter into my rest.’”
units.rightText: So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’” The Peril of Unbelief

units.leftText: Beware, brothers, lest perhaps there might be in any one of you an evil heart of unbelief, in falling away from the living God;
units.rightText: See to it, brothers, that none of you has a wicked heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God.

units.leftText: but exhort one another day by day, so long as it is called “today”, lest any one of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
units.rightText: But exhort one another daily, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by sin’s deceitfulness.

units.leftText: For we have become partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence firm to the end,
units.rightText: We have come to share in Christ if we hold firmly to the end the assurance we had at first.

units.leftText: while it is said, “Today if you will hear his voice, don’t harden your hearts, as in the rebellion.”
units.rightText: As it has been said: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion.”

units.leftText: For who, when they heard, rebelled? Wasn’t it all those who came out of Egypt led by Moses?
units.rightText: For who were the ones who heard and rebelled? Were they not all those Moses led out of Egypt?

units.leftText: With whom was he displeased forty years? Wasn’t it with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
units.rightText: And with whom was God angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?

units.leftText: To whom did he swear that they wouldn’t enter into his rest, but to those who were disobedient?
units.rightText: And to whom did He swear that they would never enter His rest? Was it not to those who disobeyed?

units.leftText: We see that they weren’t able to enter in because of unbelief.
units.rightText: So we see that it was because of their unbelief that they were unable to enter.

units.leftText: Let’s fear therefore, lest perhaps anyone of you should seem to have come short of a promise of entering into his rest.
units.rightText: Therefore, while the promise of entering His rest still stands, let us be careful that none of you be deemed to have fallen short of it.

units.leftText: For indeed we have had good news preached to us, even as they also did, but the word they heard didn’t profit them, because it wasn’t mixed with faith by those who heard.
units.rightText: For we also received the good news just as they did; but the message they heard was of no value to them, since they did not share the faith of those who comprehended it.
rightNotes: 4:2 Literally not having been united in the faith of those who heard

units.leftText: For we who have believed do enter into that rest, even as he has said, “As I swore in my wrath, they will not enter into my rest;” although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.
units.rightText: Now we who have believed enter that rest. As for the others, it is just as God has said: “So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’”

units.leftText: For he has said this somewhere about the seventh day, “God rested on the seventh day from all his works;”
units.rightText: For somewhere He has spoken about the seventh day in this manner: “And on the seventh day God rested from all His works.”

units.leftText: and in this place again, “They will not enter into my rest.”
units.rightText: And again, as He says in the passage above: “They shall never enter My rest.”

units.leftText: Seeing therefore it remains that some should enter into it, and they to whom the good news was preached before failed to enter in because of disobedience,
units.rightText: Since, then, it remains for some to enter His rest, and since those who formerly heard the good news did not enter because of their disobedience,

units.leftText: he again defines a certain day, “today”, saying through David so long a time afterward (just as has been said), “Today if you will hear his voice, don’t harden your hearts.”
units.rightText: God again designated a certain day as “Today,” when a long time later He spoke through David as was just stated: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”

units.leftText: For if Joshua had given them rest, he would not have spoken afterward of another day.
units.rightText: For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.

units.leftText: There remains therefore a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
units.rightText: There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God.

units.leftText: For he who has entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his.
units.rightText: For whoever enters God’s rest also rests from his own work, just as God did from His.

units.leftText: Let’s therefore give diligence to enter into that rest, lest anyone fall after the same example of disobedience.
units.rightText: Let us, therefore, make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one will fall by following the same pattern of disobedience. The Living Word (2 Timothy 3:10–17|2TI 3:10-17*)

units.leftText: For the word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and is able to discern the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
units.rightText: For the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

units.leftText: There is no creature that is hidden from his sight, but all things are naked and laid open before the eyes of him to whom we must give an account.
units.rightText: Nothing in all creation is hidden from God’s sight; everything is uncovered and exposed before the eyes of Him to whom we must give account.

units.leftText: Having then a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let’s hold tightly to our confession.
units.rightText: Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to what we profess.

units.leftText: For we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one who has been in all points tempted like we are, yet without sin.
units.rightText: For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin.

units.leftText: Let’s therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and may find grace for help in time of need.
units.rightText: Let us then approach the throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.

units.leftText: For every high priest, being taken from among men, is appointed for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.
units.rightText: Every high priest is appointed from among men to represent them in matters relating to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.

units.leftText: The high priest can deal gently with those who are ignorant and going astray, because he himself is also surrounded with weakness.
units.rightText: He is able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and misguided, since he himself is subject to weakness.

units.leftText: Because of this, he must offer sacrifices for sins for the people, as well as for himself.
units.rightText: That is why he is obligated to offer sacrifices for his own sins, as well as for the sins of the people.

units.leftText: Nobody takes this honor on himself, but he is called by God, just like Aaron was.
units.rightText: No one takes this honor upon himself; he must be called by God, just as Aaron was.

units.leftText: So also Christ didn’t glorify himself to be made a high priest, but it was he who said to him, “You are my Son. Today I have become your father.”
units.rightText: So also Christ did not take upon Himself the glory of becoming a high priest, but He was called by the One who said to Him: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”
rightNotes: 5:5 Psalm 2:7|PSA 2:7*; literally today I have begotten You

units.leftText: As he says also in another place, “You are a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek.”
units.rightText: And in another passage God says: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”

units.leftText: He, in the days of his flesh, having offered up prayers and petitions with strong crying and tears to him who was able to save him from death, and having been heard for his godly fear,
units.rightText: During the days of Jesus’ earthly life, He offered up prayers and petitions with loud cries and tears to the One who could save Him from death, and He was heard because of His reverence.

units.leftText: though he was a Son, yet learned obedience by the things which he suffered.
units.rightText: Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from what He suffered.

units.leftText: Having been made perfect, he became to all of those who obey him the author of eternal salvation,
units.rightText: And having been made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him

units.leftText: named by God a high priest after the order of Melchizedek.
units.rightText: and was designated by God as high priest in the order of Melchizedek. Milk and Solid Food (1 Corinthians 3:1–9|1CO 3:1-9*)

units.leftText: About him we have many words to say, and hard to interpret, seeing you have become dull of hearing.
units.rightText: We have much to say about this, but it is hard to explain, because you are dull of hearing.

units.leftText: For although by this time you should be teachers, you again need to have someone teach you the rudiments of the first principles of the revelations of God. You have come to need milk, and not solid food.
units.rightText: Although by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to reteach you the basic principles of God’s word. You need milk, not solid food!
rightNotes: 5:12 Or of the oracles of God

units.leftText: For everyone who lives on milk is not experienced in the word of righteousness, for he is a baby.
units.rightText: For everyone who lives on milk is still an infant, inexperienced in the message of righteousness.

units.leftText: But solid food is for those who are full grown, who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern good and evil.
units.rightText: But solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained their senses to distinguish good from evil.

units.leftText: Therefore leaving the teaching of the first principles of Christ, let’s press on to perfection—not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, of faith toward God,
units.rightText: Therefore let us leave the elementary teachings about Christ and go on to maturity, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith in God,
rightNotes: 6:1 Or from acts that lead to death

units.leftText: of the teaching of baptisms, of laying on of hands, of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
units.rightText: instruction about baptisms, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.

units.leftText: This will we do, if God permits.
units.rightText: And this we will do, if God permits.

units.leftText: For concerning those who were once enlightened and tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit,
units.rightText: It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the Holy Spirit,

units.leftText: and tasted the good word of God and the powers of the age to come,
units.rightText: who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age —

units.leftText: and then fell away, it is impossible to renew them again to repentance; seeing they crucify the Son of God for themselves again, and put him to open shame.
units.rightText: and then have fallen away — to be restored to repentance, because they themselves are crucifying the Son of God all over again and subjecting Him to open shame.

units.leftText: For the land which has drunk the rain that comes often on it and produces a crop suitable for them for whose sake it is also tilled, receives blessing from God;
units.rightText: For land that drinks in the rain often falling on it and that produces a crop useful to those for whom it is tended receives the blessing of God.

units.leftText: but if it bears thorns and thistles, it is rejected and near being cursed, whose end is to be burned.
units.rightText: But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless, and its curse is imminent. In the end it will be burned.

units.leftText: But, beloved, we are persuaded of better things for you, and things that accompany salvation, even though we speak like this.
units.rightText: Even though we speak like this, beloved, we are convinced of better things in your case— things that accompany salvation.

units.leftText: For God is not unrighteous, so as to forget your work and the labor of love which you showed toward his name, in that you served the saints, and still do serve them.
units.rightText: For God is not unjust. He will not forget your work and the love you have shown for His name as you have ministered to the saints and continue to do so.

units.leftText: We desire that each one of you may show the same diligence to the fullness of hope even to the end,
units.rightText: We want each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, in order to make your hope sure.

units.leftText: that you won’t be sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and perseverance inherited the promises.
units.rightText: Then you will not be sluggish, but will imitate those who through faith and patience inherit what has been promised. God’s Unchangeable Promise

units.leftText: For when God made a promise to Abraham, since he could swear by no one greater, he swore by himself,
units.rightText: When God made His promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater to swear by, He swore by Himself,

units.leftText: saying, “Surely blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you.”
units.rightText: saying, “I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants.”

units.leftText: Thus, having patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
units.rightText: And so Abraham, after waiting patiently, obtained the promise.

units.leftText: For men indeed swear by a greater one, and in every dispute of theirs the oath is final for confirmation.
units.rightText: Men swear by someone greater than themselves, and their oath serves as a confirmation to end all argument.

units.leftText: In this way God, being determined to show more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his counsel, interposed with an oath,
units.rightText: So when God wanted to make the unchanging nature of His purpose very clear to the heirs of the promise, He guaranteed it with an oath.

units.leftText: that by two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have a strong encouragement, who have fled for refuge to take hold of the hope set before us.
units.rightText: Thus by two unchangeable things in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us may be strongly encouraged.

units.leftText: This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and steadfast and entering into that which is within the veil,
units.rightText: We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure. It enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain,

units.leftText: where as a forerunner Jesus entered for us, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.
units.rightText: where Jesus our forerunner has entered on our behalf. He has become a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.

units.leftText: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
units.rightText: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,

units.leftText: to whom also Abraham divided a tenth part of all (being first, by interpretation, “king of righteousness”, and then also “king of Salem”, which means “king of peace”,
units.rightText: and Abraham apportioned to him a tenth of everything. First, his name means “king of righteousness.” Then also, “king of Salem” means “king of peace.”

units.leftText: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but made like the Son of God), remains a priest continually.
units.rightText: Without father or mother or genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, like the Son of God, he remains a priest for all time.

units.leftText: Now consider how great this man was, to whom even Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth out of the best plunder.
units.rightText: Consider how great Melchizedek was: Even the patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the plunder.

units.leftText: They indeed of the sons of Levi who receive the priest’s office have a commandment to take tithes from the people according to the law, that is, of their brothers, though these have come out of the body of Abraham,
units.rightText: Now the law commands the sons of Levi who become priests to collect a tenth from the people — that is, from their brothers — though they too are descended from Abraham.

units.leftText: but he whose genealogy is not counted from them has accepted tithes from Abraham, and has blessed him who has the promises.
units.rightText: But Melchizedek, who did not trace his descent from Levi, collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed him who had the promises.

units.leftText: But without any dispute the lesser is blessed by the greater.
units.rightText: And indisputably, the lesser is blessed by the greater.

units.leftText: Here people who die receive tithes, but there one receives tithes of whom it is testified that he lives.
units.rightText: In the case of the Levites, mortal men collect the tenth; but in the case of Melchizedek, it is affirmed that he lives on.

units.leftText: We can say that through Abraham even Levi, who receives tithes, has paid tithes,
units.rightText: And so to speak, Levi, who collects the tenth, paid the tenth through Abraham.

units.leftText: for he was yet in the body of his father when Melchizedek met him.
units.rightText: For when Melchizedek met Abraham, Levi was still in the loin of his ancestor. A Superior Priesthood

units.leftText: Now if perfection was through the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people have received the law), what further need was there for another priest to arise after the order of Melchizedek, and not be called after the order of Aaron?
units.rightText: Now if perfection could have been attained through the Levitical priesthood ( for on this basis the people received the law), why was there still need for another priest to appear — one in the order of Melchizedek and not in the order of Aaron?

units.leftText: For the priesthood being changed, there is of necessity a change made also in the law.
units.rightText: For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.

units.leftText: For he of whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has officiated at the altar.
units.rightText: He of whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.

units.leftText: For it is evident that our Lord has sprung out of Judah, about which tribe Moses spoke nothing concerning priesthood.
units.rightText: For it is clear that our Lord descended from Judah, a tribe as to which Moses said nothing about priests.

units.leftText: This is yet more abundantly evident, if after the likeness of Melchizedek there arises another priest,
units.rightText: And this point is even more clear if another priest like Melchizedek appears,

units.leftText: who has been made, not after the law of a fleshly commandment, but after the power of an endless life;
units.rightText: one who has become a priest not by a law of succession, but by the power of an indestructible life.

units.leftText: for it is testified, “You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
units.rightText: For it is testified: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”

units.leftText: For there is an annulling of a foregoing commandment because of its weakness and uselessness
units.rightText: So the former commandment is set aside because it was weak and useless

units.leftText: (for the law made nothing perfect), and a bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
units.rightText: ( for the law made nothing perfect), and a better hope is introduced, by which we draw near to God.

units.leftText: Inasmuch as he was not made priest without the taking of an oath
units.rightText: And none of this happened without an oath. For others became priests without an oath,

units.leftText: (for they indeed have been made priests without an oath), but he with an oath by him that says of him, “The Lord swore and will not change his mind, ‘You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.’”
units.rightText: but Jesus became a priest with an oath by the One who said to Him: “The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: ‘You are a priest forever.’”

units.leftText: By so much, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.
units.rightText: Because of this oath, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.

units.leftText: Many, indeed, have been made priests, because they are hindered from continuing by death.
units.rightText: Now there have been many other priests, since death prevented them from continuing in office.

units.leftText: But he, because he lives forever, has his priesthood unchangeable.
units.rightText: But because Jesus lives forever, He has a permanent priesthood.

units.leftText: Therefore he is also able to save to the uttermost those who draw near to God through him, seeing that he lives forever to make intercession for them.
units.rightText: Therefore He is able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.

units.leftText: For such a high priest was fitting for us: holy, guiltless, undefiled, separated from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;
units.rightText: Such a high priest truly befits us — One who is holy, innocent, undefiled, set apart from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.

units.leftText: who doesn’t need, like those high priests, to offer up sacrifices daily, first for his own sins, and then for the sins of the people. For he did this once for all, when he offered up himself.
units.rightText: Unlike the other high priests, He does not need to offer daily sacrifices, first for His own sins and then for the sins of the people; He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself.

units.leftText: For the law appoints men as high priests who have weakness, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son forever who has been perfected.
units.rightText: For the law appoints as high priests men who are weak; but the oath, which came after the law, appointed the Son, who has been made perfect forever.

units.leftText: Now in the things which we are saying, the main point is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
units.rightText: The point of what we are saying is this: We do have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven,

units.leftText: a servant of the sanctuary and of the true tabernacle which the Lord pitched, not man.
units.rightText: and who ministers in the sanctuary and true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by man.

units.leftText: For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices. Therefore it is necessary that this high priest also have something to offer.
units.rightText: And since every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices, it was necessary for this One also to have something to offer.

units.leftText: For if he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, seeing there are priests who offer the gifts according to the law,
units.rightText: Now if He were on earth, He would not be a priest, since there are already priests who offer gifts according to the law.

units.leftText: who serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, even as Moses was warned by God when he was about to make the tabernacle, for he said, “See, you shall make everything according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain.”
units.rightText: The place where they serve is a copy and shadow of what is in heaven. This is why Moses was warned when he was about to build the tabernacle: “See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.” The New Covenant (Jeremiah 31:26–40|JER 31:26-40*)

units.leftText: But now he has obtained a more excellent ministry, by as much as he is also the mediator of a better covenant, which on better promises has been given as law.
units.rightText: Now, however, Jesus has received a much more excellent ministry, just as the covenant He mediates is better and is founded on better promises.

units.leftText: For if that first covenant had been faultless, then no place would have been sought for a second.
units.rightText: For if that first covenant had been without fault, no place would have been sought for a second.

units.leftText: For finding fault with them, he said, “Behold, the days are coming”, says the Lord, “that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah;
units.rightText: But God found fault with the people and said: “Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
leftNotes: 8:8 “Behold”, from “ἰδοὺ”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; for they didn’t continue in my covenant, and I disregarded them,” says the Lord.
units.rightText: It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not abide by My covenant, and I disregarded them, declares the Lord.

units.leftText: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days,” says the Lord: “I will put my laws into their mind; I will also write them on their heart. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
units.rightText: For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the Lord. I will put My laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be My people.

units.leftText: They will not teach every man his fellow citizen and every man his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ for all will know me, from their least to their greatest.
units.rightText: No longer will each one teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.

units.leftText: For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness. I will remember their sins and lawless deeds no more.”
units.rightText: For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more.”

units.leftText: In that he says, “A new covenant”, he has made the first obsolete. But that which is becoming obsolete and grows aged is near to vanishing away.
units.rightText: By speaking of a new covenant, He has made the first one obsolete; and what is obsolete and aging will soon disappear.
rightNotes: 8:13 Literally In saying new; here and in Hebrews 9:1|HEB 9:1* and 18, covenant is included for clarity but is not contained in the Greek. A broader interpretation could also include priesthood or tabernacle.

units.leftText: Now indeed even the first covenant had ordinances of divine service and an earthly sanctuary.
units.rightText: Now the first covenant had regulations for worship and also an earthly sanctuary.
rightNotes: 9:1 Literally the first; also in verse 18; see the footnote for Hebrews 8:13|HEB 8:13*.

units.leftText: For a tabernacle was prepared. In the first part were the lamp stand, the table, and the show bread, which is called the Holy Place.
units.rightText: A tabernacle was prepared. In its first room were the lampstand, the table, and the consecrated bread. This was called the Holy Place.
rightNotes: 9:2 Or the Bread of the Presence

units.leftText: After the second veil was the tabernacle which is called the Holy of Holies,
units.rightText: Behind the second curtain was a room called the Most Holy Place,

units.leftText: having a golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant overlaid on all sides with gold, in which was a golden pot holding the manna, Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tablets of the covenant;
units.rightText: containing the golden altar of incense and the gold-covered ark of the covenant. Inside the ark were the gold jar of manna, Aaron’s staff that had budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant.

units.leftText: and above it cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat, of which things we can’t speak now in detail.
units.rightText: Above the ark were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy seat. But we cannot discuss these things in detail now.

units.leftText: Now these things having been thus prepared, the priests go in continually into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the services,
units.rightText: When everything had been prepared in this way, the priests entered regularly into the first room to perform their sacred duties.

units.leftText: but into the second the high priest alone, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the errors of the people.
units.rightText: But only the high priest entered the second room, and then only once a year, and never without blood, which he offered for himself and for the sins the people had committed in ignorance.

units.leftText: The Holy Spirit is indicating this, that the way into the Holy Place wasn’t yet revealed while the first tabernacle was still standing.
units.rightText: By this arrangement the Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Most Holy Place had not yet been disclosed as long as the first tabernacle was still standing.
rightNotes: 9:8 Or the Holy Place; also in verses 12 and 25

units.leftText: This is a symbol of the present age, where gifts and sacrifices are offered that are incapable, concerning the conscience, of making the worshiper perfect,
units.rightText: It is an illustration for the present time, because the gifts and sacrifices being offered were unable to cleanse the conscience of the worshiper.

units.leftText: being only (with foods and drinks and various washings) fleshly ordinances, imposed until a time of reformation.
units.rightText: They consist only in food and drink and special washings — external regulations imposed until the time of reform. Redemption through His Blood

units.leftText: But Christ having come as a high priest of the coming good things, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this creation,
units.rightText: But when Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come, He went through the greater and more perfect tabernacle that is not made by hands and is not a part of this creation.
rightNotes: 9:11 BYZ and TR that are to come

units.leftText: nor yet through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, entered in once for all into the Holy Place, having obtained eternal redemption.
units.rightText: He did not enter by the blood of goats and calves, but He entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption.

units.leftText: For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify to the cleanness of the flesh,
units.rightText: For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean sanctify them so that their bodies are clean,

units.leftText: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without defect to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
units.rightText: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, purify our consciences from works of death, so that we may serve the living God!

units.leftText: For this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, since a death has occurred for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first covenant, that those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
units.rightText: Therefore Christ is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance, now that He has died to redeem them from the transgressions committed under the first covenant.

units.leftText: For where a last will and testament is, there must of necessity be the death of him who made it.
units.rightText: In the case of a will, it is necessary to establish the death of the one who made it,
rightNotes: 9:16 Greek diathēkē is also translated as covenant throughout this chapter.

units.leftText: For a will is in force where there has been death, for it is never in force while he who made it lives.
units.rightText: because a will does not take effect until the one who made it has died; it cannot be executed while he is still alive.

units.leftText: Therefore even the first covenant has not been dedicated without blood.
units.rightText: That is why even the first covenant was not put into effect without blood.

units.leftText: For when every commandment had been spoken by Moses to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of the calves and the goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
units.rightText: For when Moses had proclaimed every commandment of the law to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, along with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled the scroll and all the people,
rightNotes: 9:19 SBL does not include and goats.

units.leftText: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded you.”
units.rightText: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant, which God has commanded you to keep.”

units.leftText: He sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry in the same way with the blood.
units.rightText: In the same way, he sprinkled with blood the tabernacle and all the vessels used in worship.

units.leftText: According to the law, nearly everything is cleansed with blood, and apart from shedding of blood there is no remission.
units.rightText: According to the law, in fact, nearly everything must be purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.

units.leftText: It was necessary therefore that the copies of the things in the heavens should be cleansed with these, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
units.rightText: So it was necessary for the copies of the heavenly things to be purified with these sacrifices, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.

units.leftText: For Christ hasn’t entered into holy places made with hands, which are representations of the true, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us;
units.rightText: For Christ did not enter a man-made copy of the true sanctuary, but He entered heaven itself, now to appear on our behalf in the presence of God.

units.leftText: nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest enters into the holy place year by year with blood not his own,
units.rightText: Nor did He enter heaven to offer Himself again and again, as the high priest enters the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own.

units.leftText: or else he must have suffered often since the foundation of the world. But now once at the end of the ages, he has been revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.
units.rightText: Otherwise, Christ would have had to suffer repeatedly since the foundation of the world. But now He has appeared once for all at the end of the ages to do away with sin by the sacrifice of Himself.

units.leftText: Inasmuch as it is appointed for men to die once, and after this, judgment,
units.rightText: Just as man is appointed to die once, and after that to face judgment,

units.leftText: so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but to save those who are eagerly waiting for him.
units.rightText: so also Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many; and He will appear a second time, not to bear sin, but to bring salvation to those who eagerly await Him.

units.leftText: For the law, having a shadow of the good to come, not the very image of the things, can never with the same sacrifices year by year, which they offer continually, make perfect those who draw near.
units.rightText: For the law is only a shadow of the good things to come, not the realities themselves. It can never, by the same sacrifices offered year after year, make perfect those who draw near to worship.

units.leftText: Or else wouldn’t they have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, having been once cleansed, would have had no more consciousness of sins?
units.rightText: If it could, would not the offerings have ceased? For the worshipers would have been cleansed once for all, and would no longer have felt the guilt of their sins.

units.leftText: But in those sacrifices there is a yearly reminder of sins.
units.rightText: Instead, those sacrifices are an annual reminder of sins,

units.leftText: For it is impossible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins.
units.rightText: because it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

units.leftText: Therefore when he comes into the world, he says, “You didn’t desire sacrifice and offering, but you prepared a body for me.
units.rightText: Therefore, when Christ came into the world, He said: “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me.

units.leftText: You had no pleasure in whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin.
units.rightText: In burnt offerings and sin offerings You took no delight.

units.leftText: Then I said, ‘Behold, I have come (in the scroll of the book it is written of me) to do your will, O God.’”
units.rightText: Then I said, ‘Here I am, it is written about Me in the scroll: I have come to do Your will, O God.’”

units.leftText: Previously saying, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin you didn’t desire, neither had pleasure in them” (those which are offered according to the law),
units.rightText: In the passage above He says, “Sacrifices and offerings, burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not desire, nor did You delight in them” (although they are offered according to the law).

units.leftText: then he has said, “Behold, I have come to do your will.” He takes away the first, that he may establish the second,
units.rightText: Then He adds, “Here I am, I have come to do Your will.” He takes away the first to establish the second.

units.leftText: by which will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
units.rightText: And by that will, we have been sanctified through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

units.leftText: Every priest indeed stands day by day serving and offering often the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins,
units.rightText: Day after day every priest stands to minister and to offer again and again the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.

units.leftText: but he, when he had offered one sacrifice for sins forever, sat down on the right hand of God,
units.rightText: But when this Priest had offered for all time one sacrifice for sins, He sat down at the right hand of God.

units.leftText: from that time waiting until his enemies are made the footstool of his feet.
units.rightText: Since that time, He waits for His enemies to be made a footstool for His feet,

units.leftText: For by one offering he has perfected forever those who are being sanctified.
units.rightText: because by a single offering He has made perfect for all time those who are being sanctified.

units.leftText: The Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after saying,
units.rightText: The Holy Spirit also testifies to us about this. First He says:

units.leftText: “This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days,” says the Lord, “I will put my laws on their heart, I will also write them on their mind;” then he says,
units.rightText: “This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, declares the Lord. I will put My laws in their hearts and inscribe them on their minds.”

units.leftText: “I will remember their sins and their iniquities no more.”
units.rightText: Then He adds: “Their sins and lawless acts I will remember no more.”

units.leftText: Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.
units.rightText: And where these have been forgiven, an offering for sin is no longer needed. A Call to Persevere (Jude 1:17–23|JUD 17-23*)

units.leftText: Having therefore, brothers, boldness to enter into the holy place by the blood of Jesus,
units.rightText: Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus,

units.leftText: by the way which he dedicated for us, a new and living way, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh,
units.rightText: by the new and living way opened for us through the curtain of His body,
rightNotes: 10:20 Literally through the veil that is His flesh

units.leftText: and having a great priest over God’s house,
units.rightText: and since we have a great priest over the house of God,

units.leftText: let’s draw near with a true heart in fullness of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and having our body washed with pure water,
units.rightText: let us draw near with a sincere heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled to cleanse us from a guilty conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.

units.leftText: let’s hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering; for he who promised is faithful.
units.rightText: Let us hold resolutely to the hope we profess, for He who promised is faithful.

units.leftText: Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works,
units.rightText: And let us consider how to spur one another on to love and good deeds.

units.leftText: not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.
units.rightText: Let us not neglect meeting together, as some have made a habit, but let us encourage one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.

units.leftText: For if we sin willfully after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remains no more a sacrifice for sins,
units.rightText: If we deliberately go on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth, no further sacrifice for sins remains,

units.leftText: but a certain fearful expectation of judgment, and a fierceness of fire which will devour the adversaries.
units.rightText: but only a fearful expectation of judgment and of raging fire that will consume all adversaries.

units.leftText: A man who disregards Moses’ law dies without compassion on the word of two or three witnesses.
units.rightText: Anyone who rejected the law of Moses died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

units.leftText: How much worse punishment do you think he will be judged worthy of who has trodden under foot the Son of God, and has counted the blood of the covenant with which he was sanctified an unholy thing, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?
units.rightText: How much more severely do you think one deserves to be punished who has trampled on the Son of God, profaned the blood of the covenant that sanctified him, and insulted the Spirit of grace?

units.leftText: For we know him who said, “Vengeance belongs to me. I will repay,” says the Lord. Again, “The Lord will judge his people.”
units.rightText: For we know Him who said, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay,” and again, “The Lord will judge His people.”

units.leftText: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
units.rightText: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

units.leftText: But remember the former days, in which, after you were enlightened, you endured a great struggle with sufferings:
units.rightText: Remember the early days that you were in the light. In those days, you endured a great conflict in the face of suffering.
rightNotes: 10:32 Or Remember when you were first enlightened.

units.leftText: partly, being exposed to both reproaches and oppressions, and partly, becoming partakers with those who were treated so.
units.rightText: Sometimes you were publicly exposed to ridicule and persecution; at other times you were partners with those who were so treated.

units.leftText: For you both had compassion on me in my chains and joyfully accepted the plundering of your possessions, knowing that you have for yourselves a better possession and an enduring one in the heavens.
units.rightText: You sympathized with those in prison and joyfully accepted the confiscation of your property, knowing that you yourselves had a better and permanent possession.

units.leftText: Therefore don’t throw away your boldness, which has a great reward.
units.rightText: So do not throw away your confidence; it holds a great reward.

units.leftText: For you need endurance so that, having done the will of God, you may receive the promise.
units.rightText: You need to persevere, so that after you have done the will of God, you will receive what He has promised.

units.leftText: “In a very little while, he who comes will come and will not wait.
units.rightText: For, “In just a little while, He who is coming will come and will not delay.

units.leftText: But the righteous one will live by faith. If he shrinks back, my soul has no pleasure in him.”
units.rightText: But My righteous one will live by faith; and if he shrinks back, I will take no pleasure in him.”
rightNotes: 10:38 BYZ and TR But the righteous will live by faith

units.leftText: But we are not of those who shrink back to destruction, but of those who have faith to the saving of the soul.
units.rightText: But we are not of those who shrink back and are destroyed, but of those who have faith and preserve their souls.

units.leftText: Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.
units.rightText: Now faith is the assurance of what we hope for and the certainty of what we do not see.

units.leftText: For by this, the elders obtained approval.
units.rightText: This is why the ancients were commended.

units.leftText: By faith we understand that the universe has been framed by the word of God, so that what is seen has not been made out of things which are visible.
units.rightText: By faith we understand that the universe was formed at God’s command, so that what is seen was not made out of what was visible. The Faith of Abel, Enoch, Noah (Genesis 4–9*)

units.leftText: By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, through which he had testimony given to him that he was righteous, God testifying with respect to his gifts; and through it he, being dead, still speaks.
units.rightText: By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. By faith he was commended as righteous when God gave approval to his gifts. And by faith he still speaks, even though he is dead.

units.leftText: By faith Enoch was taken away, so that he wouldn’t see death, and he was not found, because God translated him. For he has had testimony given to him that before his translation he had been well pleasing to God.
units.rightText: By faith Enoch was taken up so that he did not see death: “He could not be found, because God had taken him away.” For before he was taken, he was commended as one who pleased God.

units.leftText: Without faith it is impossible to be well pleasing to him, for he who comes to God must believe that he exists, and that he is a rewarder of those who seek him.
units.rightText: And without faith it is impossible to please God. For anyone who approaches Him must believe that He exists and that He rewards those who earnestly seek Him.

units.leftText: By faith Noah, being warned about things not yet seen, moved with godly fear, prepared a ship for the saving of his house, through which he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness which is according to faith.
units.rightText: By faith Noah, when warned about things not yet seen, in godly fear built an ark to save his family. By faith he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes by faith. The Faith of Abraham and Sarah (Genesis 15–22*; Romans 4:1–12|ROM 4:1-12*)

units.leftText: By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed to go out to the place which he was to receive for an inheritance. He went out, not knowing where he went.
units.rightText: By faith Abraham, when called to go to a place he would later receive as his inheritance, obeyed and went, without knowing where he was going.

units.leftText: By faith he lived as an alien in the land of promise, as in a land not his own, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise.
units.rightText: By faith he dwelt in the promised land as a stranger in a foreign country. He lived in tents, as did Isaac and Jacob, who were heirs with him of the same promise.

units.leftText: For he was looking for the city which has foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
units.rightText: For he was looking forward to the city with foundations, whose architect and builder is God.

units.leftText: By faith even Sarah herself received power to conceive, and she bore a child when she was past age, since she counted him faithful who had promised.
units.rightText: By faith Sarah, even though she was barren and beyond the proper age, was enabled to conceive a child, because she considered Him faithful who had promised.

units.leftText: Therefore as many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as innumerable as the sand which is by the sea shore, were fathered by one man, and him as good as dead.
units.rightText: And so from one man, and he as good as dead, came descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as countless as the sand on the seashore.

units.leftText: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them and embraced them from afar, and having confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
units.rightText: All these people died in faith, without having received the things they were promised. However, they saw them and welcomed them from afar. And they acknowledged that they were strangers and exiles on the earth.

units.leftText: For those who say such things make it clear that they are seeking a country of their own.
units.rightText: Now those who say such things show that they are seeking a country of their own.

units.leftText: If indeed they had been thinking of that country from which they went out, they would have had enough time to return.
units.rightText: If they had been thinking of the country they had left, they would have had opportunity to return.

units.leftText: But now they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
units.rightText: Instead, they were longing for a better country, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for He has prepared a city for them.

units.leftText: By faith, Abraham, being tested, offered up Isaac. Yes, he who had gladly received the promises was offering up his only born son,
units.rightText: By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac on the altar. He who had received the promises was ready to offer his one and only son,
leftNotes: 11:17 The phrase “only born” is from the Greek word “μονογενη”, which is sometimes translated “only begotten” or “one and only”.
rightNotes: 11:17 Or only begotten son or unique son

units.leftText: to whom it was said, “Your offspring will be accounted as from Isaac,”
units.rightText: even though God had said to him, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”

units.leftText: concluding that God is able to raise up even from the dead. Figuratively speaking, he also did receive him back from the dead.
units.rightText: Abraham reasoned that God could raise the dead, and in a sense, he did receive Isaac back from death. The Faith of Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph (Genesis 27–50*)

units.leftText: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, even concerning things to come.
units.rightText: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning the future.

units.leftText: By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff.
units.rightText: By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of Joseph’s sons and worshiped as he leaned on the top of his staff.

units.leftText: By faith Joseph, when his end was near, made mention of the departure of the children of Israel, and gave instructions concerning his bones.
units.rightText: By faith Joseph, when his end was near, spoke about the exodus of the Israelites and gave instructions about his bones. The Faith of Moses (Exodus 2–15*; Acts 7:20–22|ACT 7:20-22*)

units.leftText: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that he was a beautiful child; and they were not afraid of the king’s commandment.
units.rightText: By faith Moses’ parents hid him for three months after his birth, because they saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were unafraid of the king’s edict.

units.leftText: By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter,
units.rightText: By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.

units.leftText: choosing rather to share ill treatment with God’s people than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a time,
units.rightText: He chose to suffer oppression with God’s people rather than to experience the fleeting enjoyment of sin.

units.leftText: considering the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt; for he looked to the reward.
units.rightText: He valued disgrace for Christ above the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to his reward.

units.leftText: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king; for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.
units.rightText: By faith Moses left Egypt, not fearing the king’s anger; he persevered because he saw Him who is invisible.

units.leftText: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, that the destroyer of the firstborn should not touch them.
units.rightText: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch Israel’s own firstborn.

units.leftText: By faith they passed through the Red Sea as on dry land. When the Egyptians tried to do so, they were swallowed up.
units.rightText: By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as on dry land; but when the Egyptians tried to follow, they were drowned. The Faith of Many (Joshua–Malachi*)

units.leftText: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down after they had been encircled for seven days.
units.rightText: By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after the people had marched around them for seven days.

units.leftText: By faith Rahab the prostitute didn’t perish with those who were disobedient, having received the spies in peace.
units.rightText: By faith the prostitute Rahab, because she welcomed the spies in peace, did not perish with those who were disobedient.

units.leftText: What more shall I say? For the time would fail me if I told of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets—
units.rightText: And what more shall I say? Time will not allow me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets,

units.leftText: who through faith subdued kingdoms, worked out righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
units.rightText: who through faith conquered kingdoms, administered justice, and gained what was promised; who shut the mouths of lions,

units.leftText: quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, from weakness were made strong, grew mighty in war, and caused foreign armies to flee.
units.rightText: quenched the raging fire, and escaped the edge of the sword; who gained strength from weakness, became mighty in battle, and put foreign armies to flight.

units.leftText: Women received their dead by resurrection. Others were tortured, not accepting their deliverance, that they might obtain a better resurrection.
units.rightText: Women received back their dead, raised to life again. Others were tortured and refused their release, so that they might gain a better resurrection.

units.leftText: Others were tried by mocking and scourging, yes, moreover by bonds and imprisonment.
units.rightText: Still others endured mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.

units.leftText: They were stoned. They were sawn apart. They were tempted. They were slain with the sword. They went around in sheep skins and in goat skins; being destitute, afflicted, ill-treated—
units.rightText: They were stoned, they were sawed in two, they were put to death by the sword. They went around in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, oppressed, and mistreated.
rightNotes: 11:37 NE, WH, BYZ, and TR include they were put to the test,

units.leftText: of whom the world was not worthy—wandering in deserts, mountains, caves, and the holes of the earth.
units.rightText: The world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts and mountains, and hid in caves and holes in the ground.

units.leftText: These all, having been commended for their faith, didn’t receive the promise,
units.rightText: These were all commended for their faith, yet they did not receive what was promised.

units.leftText: God having provided some better thing concerning us, so that apart from us they should not be made perfect.
units.rightText: God had planned something better for us, so that together with us they would be made perfect.

units.leftText: Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us,
units.rightText: Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us throw off every encumbrance and the sin that so easily entangles, and let us run with endurance the race set out for us.

units.leftText: looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
units.rightText: Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy set before Him endured the cross, scorning its shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

units.leftText: For consider him who has endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, that you don’t grow weary, fainting in your souls.
units.rightText: Consider Him who endured such hostility from sinners, so that you will not grow weary and lose heart. God Disciplines His Sons

units.leftText: You have not yet resisted to blood, striving against sin.
units.rightText: In your struggle against sin, you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood.

units.leftText: You have forgotten the exhortation which reasons with you as with children, “My son, don’t take lightly the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when you are reproved by him;
units.rightText: And you have forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not take lightly the discipline of the Lord, and do not lose heart when He rebukes you.

units.leftText: for whom the Lord loves, he disciplines, and chastises every son whom he receives.”
units.rightText: For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and He chastises every son He receives.”
rightNotes: 12:6 Literally and He flogs every son He receives; Proverbs 3:11–12|PRO 3:11-12* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: It is for discipline that you endure. God deals with you as with children, for what son is there whom his father doesn’t discipline?
units.rightText: Endure suffering as discipline; God is treating you as sons. For what son is not disciplined by his father?

units.leftText: But if you are without discipline, of which all have been made partakers, then you are illegitimate, and not children.
units.rightText: If you do not experience discipline like everyone else, then you are illegitimate children and not true sons.

units.leftText: Furthermore, we had the fathers of our flesh to chasten us, and we paid them respect. Shall we not much rather be in subjection to the Father of spirits and live?
units.rightText: Furthermore, we have all had earthly fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them. Should we not much more submit to the Father of our spirits and live?

units.leftText: For they indeed for a few days disciplined us as seemed good to them, but he for our profit, that we may be partakers of his holiness.
units.rightText: Our fathers disciplined us for a short time as they thought best, but God disciplines us for our good, so that we may share in His holiness.

units.leftText: All chastening seems for the present to be not joyous but grievous; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
units.rightText: No discipline seems enjoyable at the time, but painful. Later on, however, it yields a harvest of righteousness and peace to those who have been trained by it.
rightNotes: 12:11 Or it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness

units.leftText: Therefore lift up the hands that hang down and the feeble knees,
units.rightText: Therefore strengthen your limp hands and weak knees.

units.leftText: and make straight paths for your feet, so what is lame may not be dislocated, but rather be healed.
units.rightText: Make straight paths for your feet, so that the lame may not be disabled, but rather healed. A Call to Holiness (1 Peter 1:13–21|1PE 1:13-21*)

units.leftText: Follow after peace with all men, and the sanctification without which no man will see the Lord,
units.rightText: Pursue peace with everyone, as well as holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.

units.leftText: looking carefully lest there be any man who falls short of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you and many be defiled by it,
units.rightText: See to it that no one falls short of the grace of God, and that no root of bitterness springs up to cause trouble and defile many.

units.leftText: lest there be any sexually immoral person or profane person, like Esau, who sold his birthright for one meal.
units.rightText: See to it that no one is sexually immoral, or is godless like Esau, who for a single meal sold his birthright.

units.leftText: For you know that even when he afterward desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no place for a change of mind though he sought it diligently with tears.
units.rightText: For you know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected. He could find no ground for repentance, though he sought the blessing with tears. An Unshakable Kingdom (Exodus 20:18–21|EXO 20:18-21*; Deuteronomy 5:22–33|DEU 5:22-33*)

units.leftText: For you have not come to a mountain that might be touched and that burned with fire, and to blackness, darkness, storm,
units.rightText: For you have not come to a mountain that can be touched and that is burning with fire; to darkness, gloom, and storm;
rightNotes: 12:18 Literally to what can be touched and

units.leftText: the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which those who heard it begged that not one more word should be spoken to them,
units.rightText: to a trumpet blast or to a voice that made its hearers beg that no further word be spoken.

units.leftText: for they could not stand that which was commanded, “If even an animal touches the mountain, it shall be stoned”.
units.rightText: For they could not bear what was commanded: “If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned.”
leftNotes: 12:20 TR adds “or shot with an arrow”

units.leftText: So fearful was the appearance that Moses said, “I am terrified and trembling.”
units.rightText: The sight was so terrifying that even Moses said, “I am trembling with fear.”

units.leftText: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable multitudes of angels,
units.rightText: Instead, you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. You have come to myriads of angels

units.leftText: to the festal gathering and assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of just men made perfect,
units.rightText: in joyful assembly, to the congregation of the firstborn, enrolled in heaven. You have come to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,

units.leftText: to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling that speaks better than that of Abel.
units.rightText: to Jesus the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.

units.leftText: See that you don’t refuse him who speaks. For if they didn’t escape when they refused him who warned on the earth, how much more will we not escape who turn away from him who warns from heaven,
units.rightText: See to it that you do not refuse Him who speaks. For if the people did not escape when they refused Him who warned them on earth, how much less will we escape if we reject Him who warns us from heaven?

units.leftText: whose voice shook the earth then, but now he has promised, saying, “Yet once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heavens.”
units.rightText: At that time His voice shook the earth, but now He has promised, “Once more I will shake not only the earth, but heaven as well.”
